title: Steps for constructing a Lewis diagram
body: The established sequence of steps for constructing the Lewis diagram of a molecule or polyatomic ion.

items.label: 1. Count valence electrons
items.meaning: Add the valence electrons of every atom, then adjust for charge: add one electron for each unit of negative charge and subtract one for each unit of positive charge.

items.label: 2. Arrange the atoms
items.meaning: Place the central atom (usually the least electronegative; never hydrogen) and join each bonded atom to it with a single bond, one shared pair.

items.label: 3. Complete the outer atoms
items.meaning: Add lone pairs to each outer atom until it has an octet (two electrons for hydrogen).

items.label: 4. Place leftover electrons
items.meaning: Put any electrons still unplaced on the central atom as lone pairs.

items.label: 5. Add multiple bonds if needed
items.meaning: If the central atom lacks an octet, move lone pairs from outer atoms into double or triple bonds.

items.label: 6. Show the charge of an ion
items.meaning: Enclose the diagram of a polyatomic ion in brackets and write its overall charge outside the brackets at the upper right.

caution: Topic 2.5 (2.5.A.1) requires students to construct Lewis diagrams but the CED does not print these steps. A correct diagram uses exactly the total valence electron count from step 1.
ced_evidence: 2.5.A.1: "Lewis diagrams can be constructed according to an established set of principles."

title: Valence electron total for a polyatomic ion
body: The Lewis diagram of a polyatomic ion must show the total valence electrons of its atoms, plus one electron for each unit of negative charge or minus one electron for each unit of positive charge.
caution: The CED does not state this counting rule; it is part of the established principles for constructing Lewis diagrams (2.5.A.1).
ced_evidence: 2.5.A.1: "Lewis diagrams can be constructed according to an established set of principles."

title: Central atoms with more than eight electrons
body: When needed to place all valence electrons, a central atom from the third period or below can have more than eight electrons around it in its Lewis diagram (an expanded valence shell); second-period atoms do not exceed an octet.
caution: Topic 2.5 does not state this rule; it is implied by the molecular geometries in 2.7.A.2.i that require five or six electron pairs around the central atom (trigonal bipyramidal, seesaw, T-shaped, octahedral, square pyramidal, square planar).
ced_evidence: 2.5.A.1: "Lewis diagrams can be constructed according to an established set of principles."
